concepts.title: The Gupta Dynasty and Its Realm

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Gupta Dynasty and Its Realm' refers to.
questions.a: From the fourth century CE the Gupta dynasty, with centres at Pataliputra and later Ujjayini, ruled much of northern India; peace, tribute and trade made their era one of tireless creativity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Gupta Dynasty and Its Realm'.
questions.a: Stable rule freed hands and minds: when granaries and roads are safe, art and science flourish.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Gupta Dynasty and Its Realm' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature' refers to.
questions.a: The Gupta era crowned Sanskrit letters: Kalidasa's plays and poems, including Raghuvamsham quoted in the chapter, set a standard of beauty and feeling that later centuries kept studying and imitating.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature'.
questions.a: A golden age speaks through its poets: Kalidasa's lines still teach that wisdom, not luxury, strengthens a kingdom.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Gupta Science, Mathematics and Nalanda' refers to.
questions.a: Gupta India computed the solar year, explored astronomy and medicine, and carried mathematics forward towards the decimal place-value system; universities such as Nalanda drew students from far lands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gupta Science, Mathematics and Nalanda'.
questions.a: The age measured the world: from eclipses to digits, Gupta learning reached far beyond its borders.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gupta Science, Mathematics and Nalanda' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Science and learning (source: gees107.txt, Science and learning)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gupta Art, Temples and Iron' refers to.
questions.a: The age raised the first stone temples, painted the Ajanta caves with matchless murals, and cast the rust-resistant iron pillar at Delhi, evidence of engineering skill beside artistic genius.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gupta Art, Temples and Iron'.
questions.a: Creativity in stone, paint and metal: Gupta art gave India forms of beauty and craft it never lost.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gupta Art, Temples and Iron' taught, and from which source text?
